1.explanation:
1. DataTable/DataTable.mdx — Shows the TableContainer API (title, description props) and how IDs would need to be generated for proper aria attributes.  
2. DataTable/migrate-to-7.x.md — Notes any recent changes to the TableContainer API around v7 that might have removed ID generation.  
3. DataTable/tools — Contains internal helpers or constants used by the DataTable component; useful for tracing how title/description props are applied.  
4. DataTable/stories/dynamic-content — Live example of DataTable.TableContainer with title/description; use this to reproduce the exact markup.  
5. DataTable/stories/expansion — Another story showing TableContainer usage; confirms consistent behavior across variants.  
6. DataTable/next/dynamic-content — Next-version example of dynamic content in DataTable; can illustrate whether upcoming versions address ID generation for aria labels.
1.bug_scenario:
The screenshots show a Carbon DataTable rendered inside a TableContainer with visible “Table title” and “Table description,” but no IDs are generated for these nodes. When a screen reader (JAWS) encounters the table, it falls back to reading the table’s first row (“NameDescription namedescription 2×2”) instead of announcing the container’s title/description. In a second screenshot, after manually combining title and description into a single aria-label on the container, JAWS reads “Table title Table description data table toolbar 2×2,” showing that without per-node IDs for aria-labelledby/aria-describedby the title/description cannot be referenced individually. Key elements involved are:
- The TableContainer wrapper and its title/description nodes
- The underlying <table> element rendered by DataTable
- The way aria-labelledby/aria-describedby would hook into those nodes
- The fallback labeling behavior of the screen reader when IDs are missing
